_comment:
'Incarnate. This card's attacks get go again. Blood Debt' - a Zombie Ally whose entire text is keywords plus one keyword-scoping sentence.

ALL THREE printed keywords (Incarnate, GoAgain, BloodDebt) are in printed_keywords and fire from the card DB keywords field - deliberately NOT authored here; authoring them again is a defect. The triage pass identified zero primitives, consistent with that: there is nothing beyond keywords to express.

'This card's attacks get go again' is delivered by the printed GoAgain keyword, verified end-to-end: when the ally attacks it becomes combat.attack_card (attacks are stack entries, engine.py:422-423; allies are offered as attack actions from player.allies, play.py:264), and _recalculate_attack_power stage 6 seeds combat.keywords from the ATTACK CARD's own keywords (engine.py:1903, 1930), which the resolution step pays at chain close (engine.py:721). Unconditional in, unconditional out - exactly the printed sentence.

Deliberately NOT the SOURCE_IS_ATTACK conditional-keyword shape: loader.conditional_keywords() exists for texts that GATE the keyword ('if <condition>, this gets go again'); nothing gates this one, so stripping the printed keyword and re-granting it under a WHILE_STATIC would be equivalent behaviour with more moving parts and one more thing to break.

KNOWN ARTIFACT, not fixable in JSON: played from hand, the corpse resolves as a non-attack card layer and engine.py:2322 pays +1 action point off raw card.has_go_again - but the printed text scopes go again to its ATTACKS only. This is DB flattening (the same defect class .review/angelic_descent_yellow records as 'defect is in card_data/slug_index.json, not in the JSON implementation'): loader.conditional_keywords cannot reach the layer channel (the blade_runner_yellow draft analysis), so no authoring shape suppresses it. If reviewers want the printed behaviour exact, the fix is dropping GoAgain from this slug's DB keywords - outside this file's scope.
